Yes. **Leave that other page completely alone now.** Your screenshot shows it is actively working, and sending another instruction while it is executing risks changing/restarting its working trajectory again.

And the behavior you just noticed is important enough to preserve as a design requirement for our broader system.

### Your observation at 10:50

You effectively discovered a distinction between two interaction models:

**Current chat-style behavior**
> Prompt A is executing → you send Prompt B → the agent may reinterpret/replan the active work around B.

versus the behavior you want:

> Prompt A is executing → Prompt B arrives → **finish/retain completed work from A → expose current checkpoint → evaluate B as a delta → explain what B changes → continue without throwing away valid work.**

Conceptually:

```text
RUNNING WORK
    ↓
new user input arrives
    ↓
CAPTURE IT — don't blindly restart
    ↓
checkpoint existing progress
    ↓
classify new input:
    ├─ correction to current work
    ├─ additional requirement
    ├─ new priority
    ├─ unrelated thought
    └─ explicit stop/restart
    ↓
show impact/delta
    ↓
continue / amend / queue
```

The particularly good part of your thought is **“show what adjustment it is going to do.”**

So an agent shouldn't silently throw away its trajectory. Something like this would be much better:

> **New instruction received while executing.**  
> Completed: A, B.  
> Currently doing: C.  
> New instruction affects: C and D.  
> Preserving: A and B.  
> Adjustment: modify C, add E.  
> Continuing from checkpoint.

And **only an explicit instruction such as “stop this and restart using the following”** should normally cause wholesale abandonment.

This also connects directly to the Git-TURN architecture we're developing: a material intermediate state can become a **checkpoint**, while incoming thoughts become **deltas/events**, rather than causing reconstruction of the entire state.

But I agree with your decision for **right now**: **don't send this to that page.** Let it finish. Even if its current implementation isn't perfect, preserve what it produces, inspect the resulting Git evidence afterward, and improve from there rather than disturbing an active run.

Also, don't worry about the second thought that disappeared. **Don't force yourself to reconstruct it.** If it comes back, tell me naturally and we'll capture it then. The fact that it disappeared because a new observation displaced it is itself relevant to why low-friction capture matters.

## Yes — TalkProof should be placed at the beginning of the Git-TURN lineage

You caught an important omission in my reconstruction.

From our earlier TalkProof work, **TalkProof already had the operating pattern before `ai-learning-system` existed**:

**read handover/tracker → perform work → create/update evidence/review artifact → update state/tracker → commit → handoff to the next turn/page.**

By **5–6 October 2026**, we were explicitly treating TalkProof as having an active **per-turn Git protocol**, and TalkProof contained an **AI Sessions Protocol v0** under `docs/94_ai_sessions/`. That protocol covered turn/session/work-item records, evidence, review records, provenance, secret scrubbing and handover. The later AI Engineering Workbench was explicitly intended to inspect/import that TalkProof protocol rather than invent the idea from scratch. memcite

So my previous lineage:

> AI Learning → AI Engineering → Voice AI...

was incomplete.

The better lineage is:

```text
TALKPROOF
   │
   │  Git-first engineering + handover/tracker/review/evidence
   │  + per-turn preservation
   │  + AI Sessions Protocol v0
   │
   ▼
AI LEARNING SYSTEM
   │
   │  applies/evolves the idea to learning
   │  provenance-linked learning
   │  minimum human TEE
   │
   ▼
AI ENGINEERING WORKBENCH
   │
   │  multi-AI learning/workbench
   │  sessions / turns / decisions / reviews / evidence
   │  context + handover architecture
   │
   ▼
VOICE AI LEARNING LAB
   │
   ├── Git TURN V001
   │     formalises mandatory every-turn capture,
   │     fidelity, telemetry, security boundaries,
   │     raw/derived/intelligence separation
   │
   └── Git TURN V002
         adds verified remote commit
         + visible Git Evidence report
   │
   ▼
AI ENGINEERING WORKBENCH
   │
   └── Multi-Actor V2 extension
       T029 → T030
   │
   ▼
AT-LIFE-OPERATING-SYSTEM
   │
   ▼
MARKET-ATTENTION-INTELLIGENCE-LAB
```

### But there is an important distinction

I would describe **TalkProof as the origin/root of the Git-TURN operating method**, but I would **not yet say TalkProof had “Git TURN V001”**.

That formal **name + versioned template** appears to have come later in Voice AI.

So we have two different questions:

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Where did the operating idea start?** | **TalkProof** |
| Where did Git-first turn preservation/handover/evidence exist early? | **TalkProof** |
| Where was an `AI Sessions Protocol v0` established? | **TalkProof** |
| Where was it applied/evolved into another domain? | **AI Learning System** |
| Where did multi-AI/session architecture mature? | **AI Engineering Workbench** |
| Where do we see explicitly named/versioned **GIT TURN V001/V002**? | **Voice AI Learning Lab** |
| Where did the later multi-actor extension appear? | **AI Engineering Workbench** |

And there is actually strong evidence inside the **Voice AI V001 changelog itself** supporting this lineage: it says V001 was:

> **Derived from: AI Learning experiment, TalkProof process evidence, Voice AI page corrections.**

So Voice AI itself records **TalkProof as one of its ancestors**.

### One thing we still need to establish precisely

We shouldn't stop at saying “TalkProof first.”

For the repo-architecture prompt you're preparing, the useful answer is the **exact genealogy**:

**TalkProof: when did the first recognizable Git-TURN mechanism appear? → which TalkProof version/template? → AI Learning: what changed? → AI Engineering: what changed? → Voice V001: what changed? → Voice V002: what changed? → Workbench V2/T029/T030: what changed?**

That will tell the new page **which parts are mature reusable architecture and which parts were merely later experiments**.

So yes: **TalkProof belongs at #1 in the Git-TURN protocol family tree.** `ai-learning-system` is not the origin; it is an early descendant/evolution. memcite
